title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
This incident shows an autonomous vehicle fleet deployed without adequate reserves for foreseeable traffic scenarios. On a major holiday with expected congestion near a popular destination, multiple vehicles ran out of battery power and became immobilized on city streets, requiring towing assistance. The failure occurred in the operational deployment layer, where no system existed to route vehicles to charging stations or off active roads when traffic conditions threatened battery depletion.

The vehicles were used in conditions their battery capacity could not sustain. Heavy traffic volume and unexpected road closures created a scenario that should have triggered either route changes, station repositioning, or service suspension, but none of these safeguards activated in time. A human dispatcher with authority to remove vehicles from service before they stranded would have prevented the gridlock impact.

It is not established whether the fire that resulted from driving over fireworks was caused by a sensor or decision-making failure, or whether Waymo's systems could have detected and avoided the debris.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Several Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded in San Francisco on Saturday following Fourth of July fireworks celebrations near the Golden Gate Bridge. Heavy traffic, high volumes of travelers, and unexpected road closures caused extreme congestion that drained the vehicles' batteries. Video footage showed at least a dozen Waymo cars, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets with some requiring towing. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, though no injuries were reported. Frustrated drivers spent hours in traffic as people exited their cars to complain about the stationary autonomous vehicles.

Waymo said its roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles and indicated it would evaluate ways to improve resilience during major traffic disruptions. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to discuss the incident with stakeholders to prevent similar delays in future events. This incident follows a previous December incident where a power outage caused some Waymo vehicles to stop at non-functioning traffic lights throughout the city.
